title: Deflect light past a mass
hook: Change lens mass and predict small deflection angle.
misconception: small deflection angle stays fixed when lens mass doubles.
objective: Apply α ≈ 4GM/(c²b) to compare small deflection angle when lens mass changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With weak-field light deflection by a spherical mass at fixed impact parameter, α ≈ 4GM/(c²b). When lens mass doubles, small deflection angle becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model α ≈ 4GM/(c²b); scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider weak-field light deflection by a spherical mass at fixed impact parameter, with a nonzero initial result. If lens mass triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on small deflection angle?
recall.why: Apply α ≈ 4GM/(c²b) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
